newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo Trucks sets up S.Korea subsidiary.
newsitem.headline: Volvo Trucks sets up S.Korea subsidiary.

text.p: Swedish vehicle maker AB Volvo said on Friday that its truck division was setting up a subsidiary in South Korea, establishing a sales and service network.

"The establishment of a wholly-owned subsidiary, Volvo Truck Korea Ltd, will make it possible to create a distribution structure throughout the country to reach sales of some 400 trucks by the year 1998," Volvo Truck said in a statement.

Volvo Truck said it would introduce the Volvo FH series to South Korea in June this year after the company conducted a large number of trials and quality tests in 1996 to find the right product for the Korean market.
"Using the FH12, we expect to sell some 150 trucks this year," said Peter Lindback, president of Volvo Truck Korea Ltd.
"We shall then sell 400 trucks in 1998 and plan to increase sales still further in 1999."
Volvo Truck said it would contract five workshops from the start to service Volvo trucks and there would be about 10 parts dealers.
The centre of the service network would be Osan, 40 kms south of Seoul.
The facility will also include a service school and a store for Volvo's newly-built parts.
Volvo will also start three emergency teams, called Action Service, to provide on/off road service which, in the longer term, will be increased to six.
Volvo started operating in Korea in 1989 and since then it has sold more than 1,700 trucks there.
In 1996 the total market for heavy trucks was 19,432 units of which 3,255 were tractors and 2,082 dumpers -- the segments Volvo will focus on.
The total market is expected to grow to 20,580 units in 1997, Volvo said.
